title: pr-52984-add-vpc-control-plane-provisioning-subnets-endpoints-peering-dns
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds Terraform module and examples for provisioning the Private Control Plane VPC: subnets, interface and gateway endpoints, security groups, VPC peering to customer VPCs, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. No user-visible API changes.
body: Summary: Add a reusable Terraform module and example usage to provision a VPC for Redwood Private Control Plane deployments. The module creates public and private subnets (AZ-aware), NAT gateways, recommended security groups for control-plane services, VPC interface and gateway endpoints (S3, ECR, KMS, STS, CloudWatch, Secrets Manager), VPC peering configuration with optional route propagation, and a Route53 private hosted zone with delegation records. Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private require a repeatable, security-hardened VPC pattern that supports both cloud-hosted and customer-peered control planes. This PR bundles a tested module plus a terse example and CI checks so infra teams can adopt the pattern and reference it from the Private installer. Motivation: reduce manual networking work, avoid support incidents caused by missing endpoints/security rules, and provide a canonical peering + DNS setup for control plane discovery. What changed: 1) terraform/modules/vpc_control_plane/* - new module implemented (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, security.tf) with input flags: enable_peering, customer_vpc_cidr, enable_route53_delegation, endpoints_list. 2) terraform/examples/private-control-plane-example/main.tf - opinionated example showing cross-account peering and Route53 delegation using AWS Resource Access Manager and VPC peering fallback. 3) docs/installer/vpc-provisioning.md - high-level guide and checklist for on-prem/cloud operators. 4) helm/charts/private-control-plane/values.schema.json - minor tweak to include expected control plane VPC tags to align with terraform outputs. 5) test/terraform/vpc_integration_test.sh - integration smoke tests that run terraform validate/plan with mocked variables. Checklist: [x] Module implements AZ-aware subnet distribution and NAT placement [x] Creates recommended interface/gateway endpoints for required AWS services [x] Provides secure SGs with least-privilege ingress rules for control-plane pods [x] Route53 private hosted zone and delegation record creation supported [x] Example demonstrates cross-account peering and import steps [x] Terraform docs and usage notes included Breaking changes: none. Rollout plan: merge to main, tag module v0.1.0, notify Private installer team to bump module ref and run the example in a staging account. Testing: ran terraform validate, tflint, and integration smoke test in CI; manual validation in a sandbox account to confirm DNS delegation and peering flows. Related: ENG-5273, PM-312, SUP-987. Notes: We intentionally default enable_peering=false; operators must opt in and provide customer VPC IDs to avoid accidental peering in shared environments.

merge_commit_summary: Add vpc_control_plane terraform module and example for control plane provisioning; docs and CI
changelog_entry: Added a new Terraform module (vpc_control_plane) and example to provision a secure VPC for Redwood Private Control Plane workloads. Creates subnets, endpoints, security groups, optional peering, and Route53 delegation. No behavioral changes to the API.
notes_for_ops: Operators should run the example in a staging account before production. Default behavior does not enable automated peering; enable_peering must be set and customer_vpc_id provided. When delegating Route53, ensure appropriate cross-account role permissions are configured as shown in docs/installer/vpc-provisioning.md.
observability_impacts: Adds tags to VPC and subnets for cost allocation and observability. No direct changes to control-plane metrics; recommended to update Console dashboards to filter by new vpc_tag:private-control-plane.
security_notes: Module enforces least-privileged security group defaults and creates endpoints to avoid egress to the public internet for control-plane dependencies. KMS key usage limited via policy examples in docs. Customers must supply their own KMS key or use the provided example key with key rotation guidance.
testing_notes: CI runs terraform validate, tflint, and a plan-only integration smoke test. We recommend an additional manual apply in a sandbox account to validate peering and DNS delegation end-to-end before production rollout.
